additional_info.subject: ID0469828-DC/Si-D/TR-[MP / R3 170001548] Cable is detached from plastic (Quality problem) CRM:03042000309
additional_info.body:
Hi guys, good afternoon :)
RC-TR reported several chargers with this problem:
As you can see the rubber is detaching from the cable/plug.
Do we have any kind of instructions on how to fix this? The RC mentioned that they always resorted to replacing the whole cable and I have another RC that said "
what I heard from customer, they are just pushing it back and maybe tightening that nut inside the rear socket inlet"
What should be the go-to here?
Thank you for your patience and support as always.
BR,
Francisco

additional_info.subject: RE: ID0469828-DC/Si-D/TR-[MP / R3 170001548] Cable is detached from plastic (Quality problem) CRM:03042000309
additional_info.body:
Hi Francisco,
This topic is known at product care,
On the product care card, I’m not finding relevant instructions on how to repair it
I reported this ticket on that same card right now for additional statistical reinforcement of the case,
But as a containment I would say the “go-to” would be to replace it if the cable would be still under warranty so there’s a possibility to report to supplier the case under warranty, but it isn’t since the factory warranty ended on 24/04/2025 for this charger.
So, for added flexibility with end costumer, if RC assumes the risk and has technical competences to repair it by “
pushing
it back and maybe tightening that nut inside the rear socket inlet
” maybe go with that.
However, I inform you that I’m not aware of this type of instructions (would appreciate if anyone have, to share it with us also)

additional_info.subject: ID0469828-DC/Si-D/TR-[MP / R3 170001548] Cable is detached from plastic (Quality problem) CRM:03042000309
additional_info.body:
Hi Mert, good afternoon
The answer from Product Care is that the cable needs to be replaced as there is no instructions available for this 250A cable.
Since the charger is out of warranty, you can try what I mentioned before from another colleague: "
pushing it back and maybe tightening that nut inside the rear socket inlet"
If you believe that this is affecting a lot of chargers in your country or might affect in the future, feel free to reach out to QM or PLM for further support.
From our side, the solution is given, so I will close the ticket.
If you need any help feel free to reach out via Teams.
Have a nice weekend!
Best regards,
Francisco
